subtype: Telling the truth to a friend at a price [Actor]
passage:
Thursday, 9 p.m.
Today was bad. I'll write it all down.
Yesterday I borrowed Bhupen's new cycle to go to the stationery shop and hit the kerb near the temple. The front wheel bent. Pratik and Imran were with me. Pratik said, "Just park it back. He'll think it happened in the stand. Nobody will know."
All night I kept seeing Bhupen's face when his dad brought it home.
So this morning before school I told him. "I bent your wheel. It was me, not the stand. I'll pay from my savings."
He went red and shouted, "You KNEW I just got it!" He didn't talk to me all day. At lunch the cricket group sat at the other end, and Pratik said I was "stupid for telling".
It really hurt, eating alone.
But on the way home I realised I wasn't scared anymore. I didn't have to remember any story.
Chaitanya

qa.q: What did Pratik suggest doing with the cycle?
qa.a: Pratik suggested parking it back so Bhupen would think it happened in the stand.

qa.q: Why did Chaitanya decide to tell Bhupen the truth?
qa.a: Chaitanya kept seeing Bhupen's face from when the cycle came home and could not live with hiding it, so guilt outweighed fear.

qa.q: Which choice cost Chaitanya most, and what did it give back?
qa.a: Owning up cost a day with Bhupen's anger and eating alone, but it gave back a feeling of not being scared and not having to remember a story.

qa.q: How might Bhupen see the honesty once his anger cools?
qa.a: Bhupen may still be upset about the wheel, but he might come to respect that Chaitanya told him directly and offered to pay.

grounding: A teenager admits to damaging Bhupen's new cycle despite peers urging a cover story, pays the price of anger and exclusion, and feels self-respect.

passage:
Anjali: ok everyone's in the new group. we split the online test questions and share answers
Anjali: avni you take Q6 to Q10
Avni: I'm not doing that
Anjali: what?? it's online, sir will never know
Avni: I'll know
Anjali: don't be dramatic. everyone's doing it
Avni: I'm not saying anything to sir. I'm just not joining
Anjali: then you'll get less marks than all of us. seriously think
Avni: I did think. I'd rather get a 12 that's mine
Anjali: wow ok
Anjali has removed Avni from the group
Avni: really?
Anjali: you're the one who didn't want to be in it
[Later]
Avni: got 13 out of 20
Anjali: we all got 19
Avni: ok
Avni: honestly it stings. but I'm glad it's mine

qa.q: How many marks did Avni get?
What does "honestly it stings" show about how Avni feels?
qa.a: It shows Avni feels hurt by being left out and by the lower mark, even while being glad the score is truly Avni's own.

qa.q: What made Avni's refusal clear without starting a fight?
qa.a: Avni said no simply, gave a personal reason, promised not to report anyone, and did not argue back when removed from the group.

qa.q: How might Anjali see Avni's refusal?
qa.a: Anjali seems to feel judged or annoyed, which is why Anjali calls Avni dramatic and removes Avni from the group, though Avni never accused anyone.

grounding: A teenager refuses to join a group sharing answers in an online test, is removed from the group and scores lower, and feels the sting and the self-respect together.
